card.title: IJN SHINANO

card.flavorText: IJN Shinano was a Yamato-class aircraft carrier of the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) during WWII. It was the largest aircraft carrier ever built at the time. Initially, Shinano was laid down as a third Yamato-class battleship, but due to the increasing need for aircraft carriers, it was converted into an aircraft carrier during construction. Shinano had an impressive size and displacement, with a length of over 244 meters (800 feet) and a full load displacement of approximately 72,000 tons. It was equipped with a powerful propulsion system, capable of reaching speeds of up to 27 knots. The carrier was intended to play a crucial role in Japan's naval operations, but it was completed late in the war. Shinano embarked on its maiden voyage in November 1944, but it was unfortunately sunk by a submarine, USS Archerfish, on November 29, 1944, just ten days after its commissioning. The sinking of Shinano was a significant blow to Japan's naval capabilities, as it lost its largest and most advanced aircraft carrier. The ship's fate remains an interesting episode in naval history, representing the brief operational period of a formidable carrier that never had the opportunity to fulfill its intended role in combat.
